full_source_scope.scope:
Original Theorem 1.1 only in the positive-integer $a,b,c,d$ scope, retaining both coprimality conditions, $ad-bc
e0$, fixed $C
e0$, nonzero coincidences and divergent reciprocal sum over primes with $|f_1(p)|
e1$. The conclusion is logarithmic density zero. The exact original closed-unit-disc, zero-value archimedean projection and Fourier-phase conventions in proof-ideas 1.1.2 are retained. The full original theorem is printed without rewriting its broader coefficient wording, followed by every required original background statement and all archimedean, character-elimination, sumset, approximate-Cauchy and final proof chains. Ordinary named prerequisites: Granville--Soundararajan [5, Lemma 3.1] pretentious triangle inequality, Tao [17] binary logarithmic correlations as Theorem 2.2, Ruzsa [15, Lemmas 5.3 and 5.11], Koukoulopoulos [9, Lemmas 3.2 and 4.1], Mertens and elementary Fourier integration. Literal source notes: final $I_{A,j}$ lower endpoint is $e^{-2/(AB)}$ while the preceding $r_j$ interval includes negative values; the sumset definition uses $t_i\in A$, one triangle-distance term has no comma, and the last prime sum uses $X$ amid $x_j$ notation. All original expressions and complete adjacent proof are preserved, with no mathematical referee verdict or generated repair. Converse, cusp-form application, helper and parameter outcomes count zero.
full_source_scope.reason: After the precisely stated logarithmic binary-correlation theorem and ordinary pretentious-distance estimates, the remaining argument must create a positive-measure family of archimedean projections, eliminate characters uniformly across powers, extend the associated twists through continuous sumsets and apply a quantitative approximate Cauchy equation. The authored uniform-in-power closing argument is coupled to those constructions and is more substantial than an ordinary qualifying-exam application of Tao's theorem; conservative H1.
